### What does this PR do?

This PR fixes two issues in the tools/utils/mcp_clients subpackage:
- It put's an __init__.py into tools/utils/mcp_clients. So far this has been missing, which (given the current build settings) causes the entire directory to not be ignored when building the .whl.
- It actually put's the timeout parameter in tools/utils/mcp_clients/McpClientManager.py into use by awaiting client.call_tool_mcp(...) only for timeout seconds. Without that, stuck tool-executions will cause the entire ToolAgentLoop simply hang indefinitely which is especially problematic during training.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: ...
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)
  - `{modules}` include `fsdp`, `megatron`, `sglang`, `vllm`, `rollout`, `trainer`, `ci`, `training_utils`, `recipe`, `hardware`, `deployment`, `ray`, `worker`, `single_controller`, `misc`, `perf`, `model`, `algo`, `env`, `tool`, `ckpt`, `doc`, `data`
  - If this PR involves multiple modules, separate them with `,` like `[megatron, fsdp, doc]`
  - `{type}` is in `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`, `test`
  - If this PR breaks any API (CLI arguments, config, function signature, etc.), add `[BREAKING]` to the beginning of the title.
  - Example: `[BREAKING][fsdp, megatron] feat: dynamic batching`

### Test
Changes have been tested in several longer training runs with setups that were affected by the described issues before.


### API and Usage Example

No API changes

- [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/tree/main/docs).
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. If not feasible, explain why: ...
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1) in [the `verl` Slack workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/verl-project/shared_invite/zt-3855yhg8g-CTkqXu~hKojPCmo7k_yXTQ). ## Code Review

This pull request addresses two separate issues. It correctly introduces a timeout for MCP tool calls to prevent the application from hanging, which is a critical fix for stability. It also adds a necessary `__init__.py` file to ensure the `mcp_clients` subpackage is included in the build. Both changes are well-implemented. However, the critical timeout functionality is not covered by automated tests. I've added a high-severity comment recommending the addition of a regression test to ensure this fix is robust and prevent future regressions.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

This change correctly implements a timeout to prevent indefinite hangs, which is a critical bug fix. However, there are no accompanying automated tests to verify this new behavior. For a fix of this importance, a regression test is crucial to ensure the timeout works as expected and to prevent this issue from recurring in the future.

Please consider adding a unit test that mocks `client.call_tool_mcp` to simulate a long-running operation (e.g., using `await asyncio.sleep(...)`) and asserts that an `asyncio.TimeoutError` is raised when `call_tool` is invoked with a shorter timeout.

nodes.body: This would just test the behavior of asyncio.wait_for, which seems to be sufficiently tested in the asyncio lib. Also the Exception asyncio.wait_for will raise is handled by the (already existing) catch-all exception handling in verl/tools/mcp_base_tool.py. In addiition (and as mentioned in the PR description) I've tested the behavior in several training runs across the last week. Thus I don't see the urge to write a regression test here.
